item.title: Mathi Mulakitathu(Sardines in Spicy Curry)
item.dc:creator: sairamredekar09
item.content:encoded:
Description

Mathi Mulakitathu(Sardines in Spicy Curry)

Cooking Time

Preparation Time : 30

Cook Time : 10

Total Time : 40

Ingredients

Serves 4

  • Mathi (Sardines,Cleaned and Washed) 1/2 kgs
  • Fenu Greek 1/2 tsp
  • Pearl Onions 15 nos
  • Garlic Cloves 6 nos
  • ginger 1 piece
  • Curry leaves 1 sprig
  • Tomato(sliced) 1 nos
  • Salt some to taste 1 tsp
  • Tamarind(Lemon Sized diluted in water) 1 nos
  • Water 1 cups
  • Kashmiri Chilly Powder 1 tbsp
  • turmeric powder 1/4 tsp
  • green chillies 2-3 nos
  • Coconut Oil 3 tbsp

Directions

  • First of all,mix tamarind,kashmiri chilly powder and turmeric powder in a cup of water and keep it aside.
  • In a pan,heat oil and add fenugreek to it, and saute the mix by adding the pearl onions , garlic cloves,ginger.
  • To this mix add the tomato and also the cleaned sardines(mathi) along with required salt .
  • Add the spicy mix which prepared in the first step and boil it.
  • When the gravy gets thickened,add the curry leaves and take out of flame.
  • In a small vessel,crush green chillies,pearl onions in coconut oil.
  • Mix this with curry well. And its ready to serve.
  • Serves delicious with Rice

item.title: Pav Bhaji
item.dc:creator: sairamredekar09
item.content:encoded:
Description

Cooking Time

Preparation Time : 20

Cook Time : 25

Total Time : 45

Ingredients

Serves 5

  • Vegies -carrot 2 chopped
  • Capsicum 1 chopped
  • Peas 1/2cup
  • Cabbage 1 cup chopoed
  • Potato chopped 2
  • Cauliflour chopped 1/2cup
  • Tomato grated 3
  • Onion chopped 2
  • Gingrr garlic,green chilli paste 1tsp
  • Water as required or 4 cup
  • Ghee 2tbsp
  • Dry masale-red chilli powder 1tsp
  • Salt as per taste or 1tsp
  • Orange food colour 2 pinch
  • Pav bhaji masala 2 tsp or as required

Directions

  • First boil vegies
  • Mash vegies with beater
  • Now heat the pan add ghee
  • Now add onion ginger garlic paste
  • Add tomato grated and dry ingredients
  • Cook it 2 min
  • Add mashed vegies mix it well
  • Now pour water 1 cup or as required
  • Cook it for 5 min on low flame
  • Ready to serve with pav

item.title: MISAL PAV
item.dc:creator: sairamredekar09
item.content:encoded:
Description

Cooking Time

Preparation Time : 240

Cook Time : 25

Total Time : 265

Ingredients

Serves 4

  • 4 Onion paste,
  • 2 tsp gg paste,
  • 2 green chilies
  • 1/2 dry coconut paste,
  • 1 tsp Salt,
  • 1/2 tsp haldi,
  • 1 tsp red chilly pd,
  • 1 tsp kashmiri chilly pd,
  • 4 tsp Oil,
  • 1 bowl hara wattana soaked overnight or 4 hr
  • Dry spice's (4 long, 2 badi elachi, 2 tej patta, 1/2 inch cinnamon stick, star anise),
  • 2 tomatoes puree.
  • 2 tsp misalpav masala
  • 1 bowl Farsan

Directions

  • in cooker add water n wattana n keep on flame till 4/5 whistle
  • Keep to cool
  • In pan add oil dry spices saute it n add onion
  • Add gg green chilly paste n saute it
  • Add tomato puree n dry masala n water n saute it till it leaves oil
  • Now add misalpav masala n adjust the gravy
  • Add wattana n boil n done
  • While severing put onions n farsan on it n sever hot with pav

item.title: Maharasthrian Special Misal pav
item.dc:creator: sairamredekar09
item.content:encoded:
Description

Maharasthrian Special Misal pav

Cooking Time

Preparation Time : 20

Cook Time : 10

Total Time : 30

Ingredients

Serves 1

  • Pav Buns 6 nos
  • Butter,some to taste(to roast Pav) 1 tsp
  • atki (Moth beans) sprouted an steamed(For Matki Usal) 1/2 cups
  • Onion (finely chopped For Matki Usal) 2 nos
  • Ginger garlic paste(For Matki Usal) 2 tsp
  • Spice paste(For Matki Usal) 2 tbsp
  • Goda Masala((Maharasthrian special goda masala, if not getting use garam masala) For Matki Usal) 1 tsp
  • turmeric powder 1/4 tsp
  • Red Chili Powder(For Matki Usal) 1/2 tsp
  • Curry Leaves(For Matki Usal) 1 sprig
  • Mustard(For Matki Usal) 1/2 tsp
  • Asafoetida(For Matki Usal) 1 pinch
  • Salt Some To Taste(For Matki Usal) 1 pinch
  • Oil some Teaspoons 1-2 tsp
  • Chopped large onion(For Kat/Tarri (Thin Gravy)) 1 nos
  • Chopped Tomatoes(For Kat/Tarri (Thin Gravy)) 2 nos
  • Grated coconut(For Kat/Tarri (Thin Gravy)) 1/2 cups
  • Garlic Cloves(For Kat/Tarri (Thin Gravy)) 4-5 nos
  • Ginger,some to taste(For Kat/Tarri (Thin Gravy)) 2-3 nos
  • Red chilli powder(For Kat/Tarri (Thin Gravy)) 1 tsp
  • Coriander powder(For Kat/Tarri (Thin Gravy)) 1 tsp
  • Cumin powder(For Kat/Tarri (Thin Gravy)) 1/2 tsp
  • Turmeric powder(For Kat/Tarri (Thin Gravy)) 1/2 tsp
  • Goda Masala(For Kat/Tarri (Thin Gravy)) 1 tsp
  • Chopped Coriander Leaves(For Kat/Tarri (Thin Gravy)) 1 tbsp
  • Salt,some to taste(For Kat/Tarri (Thin Gravy)) 1 pinch
  • Mixed Farsan(To serve the misal pavu) 1 cups
  • Poha Chivda(To serve the misal pavu) 1/2 cups
  • Finely chopped Onion(To serve the misal pavu) 1 nos
  • Chopped Coriander Leaves(To serve the misal pavu) 1 sprig
  • Lemon(cut into small wedges To serve the misal pavu) 1 nos

Directions

  • Tarri ( thin gravy):Heat oil in a pan and add chopped onions and fry untill they become brown in color.
  • Add garlic and chopped ginger and fry for sometime.
  • Add the grated coconut and fry for 3-4 min unill it turns brown.
  • Add chopped tomates, coriander and cumin powder and fry untill the tomatoes get mashed.Cool the mixture completely ad grind to a very smooth paste. Keep 1 tbsp of this mixture to prepare usal.
  • Heat oil in a kadai and add ground paste and fry again for few min and add red chilli powder,turmeric powder,goda masala an salt and fry for few min.
  • Add 2-3 cups of water and boil it for 8-10 min untill the oil starts floating up.
  • Add the chopped coriander leaves.
  • Makti Usal: To sprout Matki-soak the matki in very little water for 1 day or use a sprout maker to make sprouts.
  • Steam the matki with a pinch of salt for 10 min.
  • Heat oil in a kadai and crackle mustard seeds and add asafetida and curry leaves and fry for a min.Add chopped onions and fry untill they turn soft and add the ginger garlic paste and fry untill the raw smell goes away.
  • Add 2 tbsp pf spice paste as prepared above and saute for sometime.
  • Add the steamed beans fry for 2 min.
  • Add turmeric, red chilli powder and goda masala, salt and fry for sometime.
  • Add 1/4 cup water and cover it and cook for 5-8 min. The usal should not be watery but should have slight gravy.
  • NOTES to serve: Roast the Pav buns on tawa by applying butter (Make sure they stay soft) * in a deep plate add 2 ladles of Matki Usal and pour 1 ladle of tarri on top of it.Now add the poha chivda and layer of mixed farsan on top of it.Finally add a layer of chopped onions and coriander leaves. Serve hot with roasted buns, bowl of kat/tarri and lemon wedges. Dip the pav in tarri and eat along with the mixed misal.

item.title: Samosa Pattice Pav
item.dc:creator: sairamredekar09
item.content:encoded:
Description

An Indian Pav

Cooking Time

Preparation Time : 10

Cook Time : 10

Total Time : 20

Ingredients

Serves 1

  • Oil 1 tbsp
  • Cumin Seeds 1 tsp
  • Ginger Garlic Paste 1 tbsp
  • Green chili Paste 1 tsp
  • Red Chili Powder 1 tsp
  • Fennel Powder 1/2 tsp
  • Aamchur Powder 1/2 tsp
  • Garam Masala 1 tsp
  • Coriander Powder 1 tsp
  • MAshed Potatoes 1 cups
  • Green Peas(blanched) 1/ cups
  • Salt to taste 1 tsp
  • Fresh Coriander 1 tbsp
  • Fresh Pav 1 piece
  • Butter 1 tsp
  • Papad(for making pattice crunchy) 1 nos
  • Tomato, onion and cucumber ,sliced,each 1 nos

Directions

  • Take a pan and keep it on medium flame. Add in the oil, cumin seeds, ginger garlic paste and green chili paste.
  • Mix in the red chili powder, fennel powder, amchur powder, garam masala and coriander powder. Stir well to make the paste.
  • Add the mashed potatoes and green peas. Sprinkle some salt and mix it all well to make the filling.
  • Take a handful of the mixture and shape the filling into a pattice. Coat the pattice in crushed papad to give it a crunchy texture.
  • Shallow fry the pattice till they turn golden brown.
  • Take a heated pan add butter, garam masala, and coriander. Toss the pav in it to give it some flavor. Add in some tomatoes, onions, and cucumber if preferred.
  • Yummy samosa pattice pav is ready to be served.

item.title: Whole Wheat Spaghetti with Vegetables
item.dc:creator: sairamredekar09
item.content:encoded:
Cuisine: Italian

Food Type: Vegan

No of Portions: 4

Ingredients & Prep

   250 g  Whole Wheat Spaghetti

   200 g  Broccoli florets small

   200 g  Frozen Peas

   200 g  Courgette cut into slices

   2 Garlic cloves grated

   1 Onion chopped

   2 tbsp  Light soy sauce

   1 Veg stock or gel pot

   500 ml  Water

   1/2 tsp  Freshly ground black pepper

   2 tbsp  Olive Oil

Method

Step 1

Place water, stock cube & soy sauce into a saucepan, bring to the boil then blanch broccoli & peas for 3 mins, then remove with a slotted spoon & set aside, keep stock water.

Step 2

Cook pasta in a salted boiling water as per instructions.

Step 3

Heat a large frying pan over a med heat, fry courgette slices for 3 to 4 mins per side until light brown, remove then add onion & garlic, fry for 3 mins until soft, add blanched veg & courgette, salt & pepper, add some of the stock water to make a thin sauce, transfer cooked past onto the pan, toss & serve.

Suggestion & Tips

You can use other veg of choice.

item.title: Pasta with Butternut Sauce & Wild Mushrooms
item.dc:creator: sairamredekar09
item.content:encoded:
Cuisine: Italian

Food Type: Vegan

No of Portions: 4

Ingredients & Prep

   450 g  Butternut squash peeled

   250 g  Wild Mushrooms mix

   250 g  Pasta, any type dried

   75 g  Cashews nut roasted

   2 Garlic cloves grated

   2 Banana shallot finely chopped

   1 Vegetable stock cube or gel pot

   2 tbsp  Olive oil

   1/2 tsp  Thyme dried

   1/2 tsp  Black pepper ground

 Garnish

   sprinkle  Fresh parsley chopped

Method

Step 1

Cut butternut squash into large chunks, coat in oil & roast in the oven on a baking tray at 200'c for 25 mins until soft.

Step 2

Soak the cashews in hot water for 15 minutes until soft, drain then blend the cashews, butternut squash, vegetable stock, chopped garlic & salt in a blender until smooth to a consistence of custard, add a little water if required.

Step 3

Cook the pasta to package directions.

Step 4

Heat the olive oil in a non-stick pan large enough to add paste a sauce later over medium-high heat, chop mushroom to equal size, add to the pan & fry, without stirring, until golden brown approx. 2 minutes, Stir & continue frying until golden on the other side, remove mushrooms to a plate, then quickly fry the shallots, grated garlic & thyme until soft & transparent, add the fried mushrooms & sprinkle over some salt & pepper.

Step 5

Add the pasta & sauce & fried mushrooms, reserving some mushrooms to decorate the top. Sprinkle over some fresh chopped parsley.

Suggestion & Tips

You can use pumpkin in the autumn when available, use different herbs, select half the amount for starters.

item.title: Aloo Pakora
item.dc:creator: sairamredekar09
item.content:encoded:
• HEAT MEDIUM
  • SERVES 4
  • PREP 10 mins
  • COOK 10 mins
  • Ingredients
  • 1 medium size potato
  • 100g gram flour, sieved
  • 1 tbsp rice flour
  • Salt as required
  • ½ tsp carom seeds
  • ½ cumin seeds
  • 1 tbsp grated ginger
  • ½ tsp red chilli powder
  • 1 garam masala powder
  • Pinch of fresh coriander, chopped
  • ⅔ to ¾ cup water
  • 1 tsp chaat masala powder for sprinkling on the pakoras
  • Method
  1. Mix all the dry ingredients with water and check the seasoning, adjust if needed.
  2. Peel and slice the potatoes thinly in rounds.
  3. Heat oil for frying in a kadai or pan.
  4. Dip each potato, slice in the batter and place it gently in hot oil - fry aloo pakoras until they are golden and crisp.
  5. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels to remove excess oil.
  6. Repeat with the remaining aloo, cooking in batches. 
  7. Sprinkle with some chaat masala powder and serve with a mint chutney.

Served with

Delicious when served as a starter or as a  nibble with imlee, which is a tamarind based chutney. My children love these with just some plain old tomato ketchup to dunk into.

item.title: Aloo Tikki
item.dc:creator: sairamredekar09
item.content:encoded:
• HEAT MEDIUM
  • SERVES 4
  • PREP 20 mins
  • COOK 10 mins

Ingredients

  • 4 medium potatoes, washed with skin on
  • 1 tsp garam masala
  • 2-3 chillies, finely chopped
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 2 tbsp ginger, grated (3cm piece)
  • ½ tsp chilli powder
  • handful of fresh coriander, chopped

Batter

  • 100g KTC gram flour, sieved
  • water
  • 1 tsp cumin seeds
  • rapeseed oil for deep frying

Method

  • Place potatoes with the skin on into a pan and cover with cold water and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat and leave to cook gently until soft. Drain and cool.
  • Once cooled, peel the skin off with your fingers and discard. Grate the potatoes into a bowl and add the salt, garam masala, chilli, coriander, grated ginger, chilli powder and mix together.
  • Wet your hands, to stop the mixture sticking to your fingers and take a ball of the potato mixture. Shape into small patties or tikki, roughly 5cm in diameter and about 3cm thick.
  • Begin to heat the oil in a wok or a small pan.
  • In a separate bowl, sieve in the gram flour and gradually pour in a little water to make a thick batter then add the cumin seeds
  • Test the temperature of the oil by dropping in a little batter, if it sizzles and rises immediately then it is ready.
  • Dip one aloo tikki into the batter until it's covered and then carefully place it into the hot oil. Cook until golden brown (2-3 minutes)
  • Remove using a slotted spoon and set on kitchen paper. Repeat with the rest.

Served with

  • I like these with either a fresh zingy mint chutney on a warm sunny day or a warming chilli tomato chutney on a cosy cool evening.

item.title: Paneer Pakora
item.dc:creator: sairamredekar09
item.content:encoded:
• HEAT MEDIUM
  • SERVES 4
  • PREP10 mins
  • COOK10 mins
  • Ingredients
  • 120g paneer sliced into rectangles about 2cm wide. 14-16 slices
  • 2 tbsp yoghurt, whisked
  • 4 tbsp corn flour
  • 2cm fresh ginger
  • 1 green chilli
  • ½ tsp salt
  • 1 tbsp coriander, chopped

For Batter

  • 100g gram flour
  • 1 tsp  cumin seeds
  • 1 tsp salt
  • Pinch of baking soda
  • Water 

To Serve

  • 1 tsp chaat masala
  • Method

Marinade

  1. Mince the green chilli and ginger in a blender.
  2. In a mixing bowl, combine the yoghurt, corn flour, salt, ginger, green paste and coriander. Mix all together until you get a paste.
  3. Add the paneer and coat with the yoghurt mixture. Set aside for one hour or more.

For Batter

  1. Heat a little oil in a small pan to deep fry the pakora on a gentle heat.
  2. In a second bowl, mix the gram flour, cumin seeds, salt and baking soda.
  3. Add water slowly to make a thick  batter.
  4. To test that the oil is hot enough, put one drop of batter in the oil. The batter should form a small ball, sink and rise to the surface, but not change colour too much.
  5. Dip a marinated paneer slice into the batter so it is fully coated. Very carefully, slide it into the hot oil to start cooking. The pakoras will take about four to five minutes to cook. Turn it occasionally, until both sides are golden brown.
  6. Repeat with the remaining pakora in small batches. The pakora should be light and crisp. They are delicious when served with a sprinkle of chaat masala and a chutney.

Served with

Delicious when served as a starter or a nibble with imlee, which is a tamarind-based chutney. My children love these with just some plain old tomato ketchup to dunk into.

We don't just make food. We make people's experience. Maywood was built on the belief that food should be special, and we carry that belief into everything we do.

our story

Welcome to Tasty Recipes

Tasty Recipes is a food website that offers a large variety of recipes for all types of dishes. The website is easy to navigate and includes a wide range of categories such as appetizers, main courses, and desserts.

Each recipe on the website includes detailed instructions, photos, and nutritional information. Tasty Recipes also has a YouTube channel where they share recipe videos that are easy to follow.

Discover Our Menu

Indian cuisine is known for its rich flavors, spices, and diverse dishes. From savory curries to sweet desserts, Indian cuisine offers a wide range of options that are sure to satisfy any palate.

View Our Menu

Sample Menu

Starter

Indian starters are full of spicy and succulent tikkas, crispy pakodas and chaats that go along with refreshing and chatpati chutneys. A plate full of paneer or chicken tikka would be over in less than a minute while preparing that can be quite a task.

Main

Full of spices and herbs, an Indian thali can help boost immunity and improve gut and heart health. Spices and herbs, such as black pepper, ginger, garlic, cumin, cloves, hing, mint, curry leaves, not just provide flavour, but also have antibacterial, antifungal, antimicrobial and antiviral properties.

Dessert

Experts agree that a post-meal is the best time to enjoy dessert. When you eat dessert after a balanced meal then you can benefit from the nutrients in the meal to stabilize your blood sugar from the sweets. It is also better to eat it after a meal from a psychological standpoint.

item.title: Kaju Katli Recipe | Kaju Barfi
item.dc:creator: sairamredekar09
item.content:encoded:
Prep Time 5 minutes mins

Cook Time 15 minutes mins

Total Time 20 minutes mins

Cuisine Indian, North Indian

Course Desserts, Sweets

Diet Gluten Free, Vegan, Vegetarian

Difficulty Level Moderate

Servings 14

Ingredients

  • 1 cup cashews (whole) – 160 grams, at room temperature
  • ½ cup sugar – 100 grams
  • 5 tablespoons water
  • 1 tablespoon Ghee or coconut oil or any neutral tasting oil, optional
  • 1 teaspoon chopped rose petals or 1 teaspoon rose water or 8 to 9 strands of saffron, optional
  • Instructions 
  • Powdering Cashews
  • Powder the cashew in a coffee grinder, blender or a dry grinder.
  • The cashews should be in powdered form and not become pasty or oily.
  • Making Cashew Dough
  • On a low flame heat sugar and water in a thick bottomed or non stick pan or kadai.
  • Meanwhile grease a plate or a tray and keep aside or keep butter papers ready.
  • When all the sugar has dissolved in the water, add the cashew powder. There is no consistency in the sugar syrup required like one string or two string. Simply let the sugar dissolve in the water and then proceed with the next step.
  • Mix and keep on stirring the cashew mixture non-stop on a low flame.
  • The cashew mixture would start thickening.
  • Cook the kaju mixture for approx 7 to 9 minutes until the whole dough starts to come together.

Making Kaju Katli

  • Remove the whole lump of the kaju dough from the pan and place it on your work surface or in a bowl or plate.
  • Add the rose petals and ghee or oil to the cashew mixture.
  • When the heat in the dough is hot enough to handle, then knead the cashew mixture lightly.
  • Flatten the dough and place it on a butter paper or on a greased plate or tray.
  • Place a butter paper on top and then using a rolling pin, roll gently the dough from all sides till you reach a thickness of 3 to 5 mm in the dough.
  • Remove the butter paper and let the rolled dough cool.
  • When completely cooled, using a sharp knife cut the cashew dough giving square or diamond shapes.
  • Gently remove the kaju barfi with a butter knife.
  • Serve the kaju katli straight away or keep in an airtight container.

item.title: VEGETARIAN THALI
item.dc:creator: sairamredekar09
item.content:encoded:
TIMELINE AND PROCESS FOR THIS THALI

  • Soak
    • Soak chickpeas - 8 hours before or overnight
    • Soak Lentils - 4 to 6 hours or overnight.
    • and, soak the rice - 30 minutes
  • Cook
    • Channa masala - 40 minutes
    • Dal - 20 minutes
    • Mixed vegetables curry - 20 minutes
    • Rice - 20 minutes
  • Make chapati - 40 minutes
  • Raita - 5 - 10 minutes

Ingredients

Mixed vegetable curry

  • ⅓ tablespoon Vegetable oil
  • ⅙ tablespoon Ghee
  • ⅙ large Onions finely diced
  • ½ - ⅔ Curry leaves
  • ⅔ large Garlic cloves finely diced
  • ⅓ large Green chilies roughly chopped
  • ⅓ large Tomatoes finely diced
  • ⅙ tablespoon Chili powder I used Kashmiri chili powder
  • ⅙ tablespoon Coriander powder
  • ⅙ teaspoon Cumin powder
  • ⅛ teaspoon Turmeric powder
  • ⅛ cup Cilantro finely chopped
  • ⅓ cup Potato cut into small dice
  • ⅓ cup Carrots cut into small dice
  • ⅓ cup Frozen peas
  • ⅙ tablespoon Fenugreek leaves kasoori methi
  • ⅛ cup Coconut milk
  • ⅙ teaspoon Salt
  • ⅛ teaspoon Black pepper
  • ⅙ cup Vegetable stock or water
  • ⅙ tablespoon Lemon juice

Channa masala

  • ⅓ cup Chickpeas soaked in water for 8 hours
  • ⅓ tablespoon Vegetable oil
  • ⅙ large Onion finely diced
  • 1 large Garlic cloves finely diced
  • ½ inch Fresh ginger
  • ⅙ large tomatoes
  • ⅙ tablespoon Sweet paprika
  • ⅙ teaspoon Cayenne pepper
  • ⅙ teaspoon Cumin powder
  • ⅓ tablespoon Coriander powder
  • ⅛ teaspoon Turmeric powder
  • ⅙ cup Coconut cream or 2 cup coconut milk
  • ⅙ teaspoon Tamarind paste deseeded and chopped
  • ⅓ large Dates
  • ⅛ cup Chopped cilantro coriander leaves

Dal

  • ⅓ cup Yellow dal soaked in water for 4 to 6 hours
  • ⅓ tablespoon Vegetable oil
  • ⅙ tablespoon Ghee
  • ⅙ teaspoon Mustard seeds
  • ⅛ teaspoon Cumin seeds
  • ⅔ - ⅚ Curry leaves
  • ½ large Garlic cloves sliced
  • ⅓ med Green chilies sliced
  • ⅙ medium Onion sliced or 8 to 10 pearl onions
  • ⅙ teaspoon Turmeric powder
  • ⅓ cups Vegetable stock
  • ⅛ cup Chopped cilantro leaves coriander

Mango kudhi

  • ⅙ cup Greek yogurt Dahi
  • ⅓ tablespoon Chickpea flour Besan
  • ½ cups Water
  • ⅙ tablespoon Cooking oil
  • ⅙ tbsp Ghee
  • ⅛ teaspoon Cumin seeds
  • ⅛ teaspoon Mustard seeds
  • ⅓ large Dry red chilies deseeded and broken into pieces
  • ⅓ med Green chilies slit into two
  • ⅛ teaspoon Turmeric powder
  • ⅙ cup Mango puree
  • ⅛ teaspoon Salt
  • ⅛ teaspoon White pepper

Chapati

  • ½ cups Chapati flour
  • ⅙ cup All-purpose flour
  • ⅙ teaspoon Salt
  • ⅙ tablespoon Ghee
  • ⅛ cup Olive oil

Steamed rice

  • ⅓ cups Basmati rice soaked in water for 30 minutes
  • ½ cups Water
  • ⅙ teaspoon Salt

Raita

  • ⅓ cups Greek yogurt
  • ⅛ teaspoon Salt
  • ⅛ teaspoon Black pepper
  • ⅛ teaspoon Cumin powder

Instructions

Mixed vegetable curry

  • In a large saute pan over medium heat add the oil and ghee. Saute the onions until translucent then add the curry leaves and garlic. Next, add the chopped tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes until soft. Add, the spices and saute for 2 minutes until fragrant.⅓ tablespoon Vegetable oil,⅙ tablespoon Ghee,⅙ large Onions,½ - ⅔ Curry leaves,⅔ large Garlic cloves,⅓ large Green chilies,⅙ tablespoon Chili powder,⅙ tablespoon Coriander powder,⅙ teaspoon Cumin powder,⅛ teaspoon Turmeric powder,⅓ large Tomatoes
  • Then, add the chopped cilantro, potatoes, and carrots. Combine well and cook for 3 to 4 minutes. Next, add the green peas, fenugreek leaves, coconut mil, salt, pepper, and stock.Pro tip - we cook the potatoes and carrots first because they take longer than the peas.⅛ cup Cilantro,⅓ cup Potato,⅓ cup Carrots,⅓ cup Frozen peas,⅙ tablespoon Fenugreek leaves,⅙ teaspoon Salt,⅛ teaspoon Black pepper,⅙ cup Vegetable stock or water,⅛ cup Coconut milk
  • Cover and cook on medium-low for 8 to 10 minutes or until the veggies are tender. Add the lemon juice. Taste and adjust seasoning. Sprinkle with more chopped cilantro leaves.⅙ tablespoon Lemon juice

Channa masala

  • In a pressure cooker over medium heat add the oil and saute the onions until lightly golden. Add the ginger and garlic and saute for about a minute more.Pro tip - Alternatively, you can use an instant pot on saute mode.⅓ tablespoon Vegetable oil,⅙ large Onion,1 large Garlic cloves,½ inch Fresh ginger
  • Next, add the tomatoes and spices. Saute until the tomatoes are soft and the spices are fragrant about 2 to 3 minutes.⅙ large tomatoes,⅙ tablespoon Sweet paprika,⅙ teaspoon Cayenne pepper,⅙ teaspoon Cumin powder,⅓ tablespoon Coriander powder,⅛ teaspoon Turmeric powder
  • Next, add the soaked drained chickpeas, coconut milk, tamarind paste, and chopped dates. Season with salt and pepper and add 2 cups of water.⅓ cup Chickpeas,⅙ cup Coconut cream,⅙ teaspoon Tamarind paste,⅓ large Dates,⅛ cup Chopped cilantro
  • Cover the pressure cooker lid and add the whistle then pressure cook on high for 20 minutes about 5 to 6 whistles. Let cool for 10 minutes. Then, taste and adjust the seasoning. Garnish with more fresh cilantro.Pro tip - If you use an instant pot, switch from saute mode to pressure cook mode. Cover the lid and close the vent. Then pressure cook on high for 20 minutes. Let manual release for 10 minutes.

Dal

  • In the pressure cooker over medium heat add the vegetable oil and ghee. When hot add the mustard seeds and wait for them to splatter. Then, add the cumin seeds, curry leaves, and chilies. Add the sliced or pearl onions and saute for 2 to 3 minutes.⅓ tablespoon Vegetable oil,⅙ tablespoon Ghee,⅙ teaspoon Mustard seeds,⅛ teaspoon Cumin seeds,⅔ - ⅚ Curry leaves,½ large Garlic cloves,⅓ med Green chilies,⅙ medium Onion
  • Next, add the turmeric powder, chopped cilantro, and soaked drained lentils. Add the water and season with salt and pepper.⅓ cup Yellow dal,⅓ cups Vegetable stock,⅙ teaspoon Turmeric powder
  • Cover the pressure cooker lid and add the whistle then pressure cook on high for 10 minutes about 5 to 6 whistles. Let cool for 10 minutes. Then, taste and adjust the seasoning. Garnish with more fresh cilantro.Pro tip - If you use an instant pot, switch from saute mode to pressure cook mode. Cover the lid and close the vent. Then pressure cook on high for 10 minutes. Let manual release for 10 minutes.

Mango kudhi

  • In a small bowl, combine yogurt and chickpea flour. Add water a little at a time making sure you have no lumps. Set aside⅙ cup Greek yogurt,⅓ tablespoon Chickpea flour,½ cups Water,⅙ cup Mango puree
  • In a saute pan over medium heat add the vegetable oil and ghee. When hot add the mustard seeds and let them splutter. Then add the cumin seeds, chilies, and turmeric powder.⅙ tablespoon Cooking oil,⅙ tbsp Ghee,⅛ teaspoon Cumin seeds,⅛ teaspoon Mustard seeds,⅓ large Dry red chilies,⅓ med Green chilies,⅛ teaspoon Turmeric powder
  • Next, add the yogurt mixture. Season with salt and pepper. Let it cook on medium heat until it comes to a boil. Then reduce the heat to low and cook for 10 minutes more. Taste and adjust seasoning. Garnish with fresh cilantro.⅛ teaspoon Salt,⅛ teaspoon White pepper,⅛ cup Chopped cilantro leaves

Chapati

  • In a bowl, combine the whole wheat and white flour, salt, and ghee. Rub with your fingers until all the oil is well incorporated. Gradually add the warm water and bring the dough into a ball. Knead for 2 to 3 minutes until you have a soft dough. Cover and leave to rest for 15 minutes.½ cups Chapati flour,⅙ cup All-purpose flour,⅙ teaspoon Salt,⅙ tablespoon Ghee
  • After resting divide the dough into 8 to 10 portions. Shape each portion into a ball. Coat each ball with flour and roll into a circle about 6 to 8-inch in diameter.
  • Place a frying pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Cook each chapati on the skillet for about 2 to 3 minutes on each side. Lightly brush with oil during cooking. Keep wrapped between layers of a folded towel.⅛ cup Olive oil

Basmati rice

  • In a saucepan over medium heat add the soaked and drained rice, water, and salt. Bring to a boil and then reduce the heat to low. Cover the pot and simmer on low for 15 minutes. After 15 minutes turn the heat off and leave it untouched for another 10 minutes. Then fluff the rice with a fork.⅓ cups Basmati rice,½ cups Water,⅙ teaspoon Salt

Raita

  • In a bowl combine the yogurt, salt, pepper, and cumin powder. Taste and adjust seasoning.⅓ cups Greek yogurt,⅛ teaspoon Salt,⅛ teaspoon Black pepper,⅛ teaspoon Cumin powder
